0021d326.clue: The claim is that olms leave their caves to find food.
steps: Look for evidence connecting their food to the surface.
C says surface earthworms are a major part of their diet. That makes surface feeding more likely, so C supports the claim.
0021d326.trap: Evidence should support the specific claim, not just tell you another fact about olms.

wrong.A: Breeding frequency does not show where olms feed.
wrong.B: The number of cave systems does not show whether olms leave them.
wrong.D: Different brains do not establish surface feeding.

0021d326.subject: rw
0021d326.title: Support

01de46bb.clue: Deep water can uproot and kill the plants.
steps: Predict a simple meaning: easily affected by water depth.
B, “sensitive,” expresses that vulnerability. Read it back: the plants are extremely sensitive to water depth.
01de46bb.trap: A word must fit both the meaning and the phrase “___ to water depth.”

wrong.A: “Immune” means protected from the effect—the opposite of the passage.
wrong.C: “Limited to water depth” does not express vulnerability to changes in depth.
wrong.D: “Receptive” means open to receiving something; it does not describe damage from deep water.

01de46bb.subject: rw
01de46bb.title: Word

02e49a0c.clue: The underlined sentence says fossil studies used incomplete data.
steps: Ask what that sentence does, rather than summarizing the whole passage.
Incomplete data is a weakness in the earlier fossil studies. B describes that limitation.
02e49a0c.trap: Keep track of which studies are being criticized: fossil studies, not genetic studies.

wrong.C: It identifies a problem with turtle research; it does not summarize crocodile evolution.
wrong.D: The criticism concerns fossil evidence, not genetic studies.

02e49a0c.subject: rw
02e49a0c.title: Purpose or structure

0113152f.clue: The claim links Kelly’s decorative buttons to women he observed during childhood.
steps: The evidence needs both pieces: a female relative and buttons used for appearance.
C supplies both: his grandmother added mismatched buttons to draw attention away from clothing flaws.
0113152f.trap: Mentioning his family or his buttons alone is only half the needed connection.

wrong.A: It describes his designs without explaining their family influence.
wrong.B: It shows Kelly influencing others—the direction is reversed.
wrong.D: It connects family to sewing and drawing, not decorative buttons.

0113152f.subject: rw
0113152f.title: Quotation

01989d77.clue: Watermilfoil tanks released less methane than duckweed or algae tanks.
steps: Keep the conclusion close to the comparison the study actually tested.
A fits: underwater plants such as watermilfoil may help limit methane escaping from shallow water.
01989d77.trap: Lower emissions do not mean zero emissions, and the study did not test every possible plant arrangement.

wrong.C: The study measured methane, not how common each plant is.
wrong.D: No mixed-plant treatment was tested, so “best” is unsupported.

01989d77.subject: rw
01989d77.title: Inference

03e5cf33.clue: The hypothesis says shifting colors make iridescent wings harder to see.
steps: Predict the result before checking the choices: people should find fewer iridescent wings than solid-color wings.
A matches that prediction directly.
03e5cf33.trap: Compare iridescent wings with noniridescent wings; a comparison of blue with purple misses the hypothesis.

wrong.B: Finding iridescent wings faster would suggest they are easier to see.
wrong.C: This compares two solid colors, not iridescence with solid colors.
wrong.D: Some people finding everything does not establish which wings are harder to see on average.

03e5cf33.subject: rw
03e5cf33.title: Support

03eeecf3.clue: The wind scatters seeds; the speaker then describes scattered, painful thoughts.
steps: Connect the natural image to what follows: the unsettled seeds mirror the speaker’s unsettled mind.
C captures that movement from an observation in nature to an inner emotional state.
03eeecf3.trap: A comparison does not prove that the wind caused the speaker’s distress.

wrong.A: The poem does not say the natural event caused the speaker’s feelings.
wrong.B: Nature and the speaker are both unsettled; they are not contrasted as stable versus unpredictable.
wrong.D: The poem does not claim this self-evaluation is common to people generally.

03eeecf3.subject: rw
03eeecf3.title: Purpose or structure

0045c234.clue: The claim includes a limit: a planet contains equal or smaller quantities of its host star’s materials.
steps: To weaken that limit, find a planet with more of a material than its host star.
C gives exactly that counterexample: some rocky planets contain considerably more iron.
0045c234.trap: Shared ingredients alone do not establish the claimed limit on their quantities.

wrong.A: The composition of stars alone does not test the planet–star comparison.
wrong.B: Comparing two stars does not compare a planet with its host star.
wrong.D: A method working poorly on other kinds of planets supplies no direct counterexample to the claimed composition relationship.

0045c234.subject: rw
0045c234.title: Weaken

0198240a.clue: High pressure compresses water by destabilizing hydrogen bonds. TMAO is proposed to reduce that compression.
steps: Follow the mechanism: if TMAO keeps those bonds stable, water should better resist compression.
D reports more stable hydrogen bonds when TMAO is present, directly supporting that mechanism.
0198240a.trap: Track what must be protected: water’s structure, not TMAO’s own shape.

wrong.A: Water being impervious to TMAO does not show that TMAO stabilizes water under pressure.
wrong.B: TMAO keeping its own shape does not establish that water resists compression.
wrong.C: More TMAO paired with faster compression points in the opposite direction.

0198240a.subject: rw
0198240a.title: Support

024eb2ec.clue: The study asks whether silk properties diversified, then finds significant differences between species.
steps: Separate the background (different web designs) from the tested question (different silk properties).
B combines the study’s question and result: silk properties appear to have diversified during adaptive radiation.
024eb2ec.trap: Do not turn two kinds of variation into a claim that one caused the other.

wrong.A: The text does not compare the speed of the two changes.
wrong.C: The study does not establish that silk differences explain web-design differences.
wrong.D: It denies silk diversification, contradicting the reported differences.

024eb2ec.subject: rw
024eb2ec.title: Main idea

f5c3e3b8.clue: Multiplying powers with the same base means adding their exponents.
steps: Group each letter: m⁴ × m = m⁵; q⁴ × q⁵ = q⁹; z⁻¹ × z³ = z².
Combine them: m⁵q⁹z², which is B.
f5c3e3b8.trap: Add exponents when multiplying like bases; do not multiply the exponents.
f5c3e3b8.subject: math
f5c3e3b8.title: Exponents and roots

3c95093c.clue: Every term in 6x − 9y > 12 has a factor of 3.
steps: Divide every term on both sides by 3: 2x − 3y > 4.
That is B. Because 3 is positive, the inequality sign stays the same.
3c95093c.trap: Reverse the sign only when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.
3c95093c.subject: math
3c95093c.title: Solve a quadratic or other nonlinear equation

steps: Divide each term by 2xy: 16x³y² ÷ 2xy = 8x²y, and 14xy ÷ 2xy = 7.
Factor: 2xy(8x²y + 7), which is B.
72ebc024.subject: math
72ebc024.title: Which expression is equivalent?

beca03de.clue: Rectangle area is length × width. The expression is (15w)(w).
steps: The width is w, and the length is 15 times that width: 15w.
So 15w represents the length in feet. Choose A.
beca03de.trap: The whole product is area; one factor, 15w, is a length.
beca03de.subject: math
beca03de.title: Meaning of a number in a nonlinear model

steps: Check the middle term: 2(2a)(5b) = 20ab. It matches.
Therefore 4a² + 20ab + 25b² = (2a + 5b)². One factor is 2a + 5b, choice B.
dd4ab4c4.trap: A perfect-square pattern needs the middle term to match too.
dd4ab4c4.subject: math
dd4ab4c4.title: Which expression is equivalent?

a5663025.clue: A solution to a graphed system is a point shared by both graphs.
steps: Count the intersections of the line and the parabola. They cross once on the left and once on the right.
There are 2 solutions, so choose C.
a5663025.trap: Count intersections between the graphs, not crossings of the axes.
a5663025.subject: math
a5663025.title: How many real solutions?

d0a7871e.clue: Both expressions equal y, so set them equal to each other.
steps: x + 1 = x² + x. Subtract x from both sides: 1 = x².
Thus x = −1 or 1. Only −1 appears in the choices, so choose A.
d0a7871e.trap: “Could be” asks for one possible value; x² = 1 has two roots.
d0a7871e.subject: math
d0a7871e.title: Line meets curve

512bd5b4.clue: Increasing x by 6 increases the exponent x/3 by 2.
steps: The growth multiplier is therefore 1.20² = 1.44.
A multiplier of 1.44 means 144% of the original value, which is a 44% increase. Enter 44.
512bd5b4.trap: Two 20% increases compound: 1.20 × 1.20, not 20% + 20%. The starting factor 27 cancels in the ratio.
512bd5b4.subject: math
512bd5b4.title: Build the exponential model

f01108a8.clue: Crossing the x-axis means y = 0. The base a/7 is greater than 1.
steps: An exponential with base greater than 1 increases continuously from values approaching 0 to arbitrarily large values. Since b/9 is positive, it reaches that target exactly once. Choose B.
f01108a8.trap: The shifts change where the crossing happens, not the number of crossings here. No logarithm calculation is needed.
f01108a8.subject: math
f01108a8.title: Zeros and x-intercepts

301faf80.clue: Let the smaller integer be n; the first is 2n + 5.
steps: Their product gives n(2n + 5) = 462, or 2n² + 5n − 462 = 0.
Factor: (n − 14)(2n + 33) = 0. The positive integer root is n = 14.
Check: the first integer is 33, and 14 × 33 = 462. Enter 14.
301faf80.trap: Translate “5 greater than twice” as 2n + 5, not 2(n + 5). Reject the negative root.
